defect: Forking cup50_desk rewrote every 'from crypto_trade.cup50.' import and left six paths built from string segments untouched: five data paths and one tournament path. A path assembled from literals is invisible to an import-level rewrite, invisible to lint, and invisible to every test that does not actually build a snapshot.
family: The same shape as the rest of this edition, one layer down: a mechanism that appeared to have run and had not run everywhere, with nothing checking the property it was meant to establish.
fix: All six paths corrected. A test now asserts no desk source names another edition at all -- cup50, cup20 or top40 -- as a quoted segment or a path fragment. It immediately found the second one, which my first grep had missed because that grep looked only at data paths.
found_at_phase: first tick after launch, before any boundary was published
found_by: the first paper tick, failing to open data/cup50/is/manifest.json
how_much_worse_it_could_have_been: The desk would have replayed against CUP-50's universe and sealed extent, producing a forward record that meant nothing. It failed loudly only because this worktree has no data/cup50 directory; in a checkout that had one it would have run, for six months, confidently.
no_result_is_affected: No boundary was published. The tick failed before writing anything, which is the fail-closed behaviour working as designed.
title: the forked desk still read another edition's data
